scope: Corollary 2.10 (Propagation across a small disc) of the manuscript “Every complex K3 surface is Oka” (preprints/Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 042 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c35e20c01dcefe76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 11-12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a coordinate neighborhood contains a closed affine complex-line disc centered at x, with its boundary in the open locus where L holds. 11 Then L holds at x. In particular, if the complement of that locus is contained locally in a proper analytic subset, L holds everywhere.
